rounds.text: Chiraharit Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.29x, backed by a share price of ₹ 8.10 against a book value of ₹ 6.29 [E2], and sits near parity with a sector benchmark P/B of 1.33x [E6]. More importantly, the company boasts a proven, multi-year compounding engine with a 3-year median return on equity of 24% [E18] and a stellar 5-year median return on equity of 27% [E17], supported by an explicit positive flag for a strong ROE track record averaging 23.8% over three years [E39]. The market capitalisation stands firmly at ₹ 44.4 Cr [E3], yet the stock languishes at just 26% of the way through its 52-week range [E5], representing a severe mispricing of a fundamentally high-returning asset. Chiraharit Ltd carries a staggering valuation disconnect, trading at an extreme price-to-earnings multiple of 108 [E1]. This rich multiple stands in stark contrast to the company's deeply depressed profitability, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of 1.18% that severely trails the sector benchmark of 9.37% [E7]. Operational returns are similarly anemic, with the return on capital employed sitting at 3.59% against a sector benchmark of 11.76% [E8]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero income protection, as the dividend yield is completely absent at 0.00% [E4]. The recent collapse in profitability is highlighted by a median return on equity over the last year dropping to just 2% [E19], triggering a low ROE warning signal [E44]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a historical multi-year cushion with a median return on equity of 27% over 5 years [E17] and 24% over 3 years [E18].

Conceded: the current price-to-earnings ratio is 108 [E1], the current return on equity is a low 1.18% to 1.8% [E7, E10], the return on capital employed is 3.59% [E8], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. However, focusing solely on the recent one-year ROE drop to 2% [E19] and the resulting screen warning [E44] ignores a proven multi-year earning capacity, as demonstrated by a robust median 3-year ROE of 24% to 23.8% and a 5-year median ROE of 27% [E17, E18, E39]. This historical compounding track record proves the business has generated substantial returns through economic cycles, rendering the current single-year compression a temporary trough rather than a structural failure. Furthermore, the market capitalization sits at a modest ₹ 44.4 Cr [E3], and the stock trades at a price-to-book of 1.29x [E2], or essentially right at a sector-aligned 1x benchmark [E6], while lingering near the lower end of its range at just 26% of its 52-week span [E5]. This low valuation relative to historical earning power means investors are paying minimal multiples for depressed assets that have historically delivered extraordinary ROE performance [E17, E18].

Conceded: the 3-year median ROE is 24% to 23.8% and the 5-year median ROE is 27% [E17, E18, E39]. However, leaning on these historical figures ignores the harsh reality that current profitability has completely collapsed to a meager 1.18% to 1.8% ROE [E7, E10] alongside a dreadful 2% one-year median ROE [E19], triggering a formal low ROE screen warning [E44]. Paying a staggering P/E of 108 [E1] for a company generating such negligible present returns cannot be justified by past compounding, especially when the ROCE sits at a paltry 3.59% compared to the 11.76% sector benchmark [E8]. Furthermore, the bull points to a modest market cap of ₹ 44.4 Cr [E3] and a 26% 52-week range position [E5] as cheap entry points, but a 1.29x price-to-book [E2] with zero dividend yield [E4] offers no safety net while capital sits trapped in an asset base producing a sub-2% return [E10].
